newsitem.title: USA: Mobil gets $139 mln for Permian Basin wells.
newsitem.headline: Mobil gets $139 mln for Permian Basin wells.

text.p: Mobil Corp said Thursday its Mobil Exploration & Producing U.S. Inc subsidiary has sold interests in 27 fields in the Permian Basin of West Texas and southeastern New Mexico to Titan Resources LP for $139 million.
Based in Midland, Texas, the partnership is a Titan Exploration Inc affiliate, Mobil spokesman David Dickson said. The sale was effective September 1, 1996.
Production from the fields averaged about 9,000 barrels per day of oil equivalent in 1996, including 34 million cubic feet of gas and 3,400 barrels of oil and condensate per day.
This represents just under 10 percent of Mobil's total production in the Permian Basin, the company noted.

Mobil operated 13 of the 27 fields, which contained more than 1,557 wells, and held working interests ranging from 2.5 to 100 percent. Key fields in this sale include Mi Vida, West Seminole and Sand Hills in West Texas and Eunice in New Mexico.

This sale is consistent with the previously announced Mobil Exploration restructuring plan, which is on target to reduce annual pretax operating costs by $100 million and to sell or trade up to 50,000 barrels per day oil equivalent of non-strategic assets.
